questions.prompt: In the human female, primary oocytes are arrested from fetal life until puberty at the stage of
questions.explanation: Primary oocytes begin meiosis I before birth and stop in prophase I until ovulation. The arrest in metaphase II applies to the secondary oocyte, which finishes meiosis only if fertilised.

questions.prompt: Fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The ampulla is the widest, lateral part of the tube, and the egg and sperm usually meet there. The isthmus is the narrow medial part, so it is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Which event enables sperm to penetrate the zona pellucida of the oocyte?

options.text: The cortical reaction of the oocyte
The acrosome reaction, releasing enzymes such as hyaluronidase and acrosin

questions.explanation: Enzymes released from the acrosome digest a path through the zona. The cortical reaction happens after entry and blocks further sperm.

questions.prompt: The cortical reaction after fusion of the first sperm with the oocyte serves to
questions.explanation: Cortical granules release enzymes that alter the zona so that other sperm cannot bind. Polyspermy would give an abnormal chromosome number.

questions.prompt: The solid ball of 12 to 32 blastomeres that forms about three to four days after fertilisation is the
questions.explanation: A morula is a solid mass of cells formed by cleavage. The blastocyst, which is the next stage, has a fluid-filled cavity.

questions.prompt: In the blastocyst, the inner cell mass (embryoblast) gives rise to
questions.explanation: The inner cell mass forms the embryo. The trophoblast, the outer cell layer, forms the embryonic part of the placenta.

questions.prompt: Implantation of the human blastocyst begins about
questions.explanation: The blastocyst attaches to the endometrium about the end of the first week. The 3-week point is when gastrulation occurs instead.

questions.prompt: The most common site of ectopic pregnancy is the
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg may implant in the tube where it was fertilised. Tubal rupture is a surgical emergency. Implantation in the upper body of the uterus is normal, so a pregnancy there is not ectopic. Ovarian and cervical sites are rare.

questions.prompt: The hormone detected in routine pregnancy tests, secreted by the syncytiotrophoblast, is
questions.explanation: hCG maintains the corpus luteum in early pregnancy and appears in maternal urine. Progesterone is raised in pregnancy but is not unique to it, so it is unsuitable as the test marker.

questions.prompt: During the second week of development, the embryonic disc is made up of

options.text: three layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm
two layers: the epiblast and the hypoblast

questions.explanation: The bilaminar disc has the epiblast and hypoblast. The three germ layers appear in the third week, after gastrulation.

questions.prompt: Gastrulation, which converts the bilaminar disc into a trilaminar disc, occurs in
questions.explanation: Cells of the epiblast migrate through the primitive streak and form the three germ layers during week 3. Week 1 covers fertilisation and cleavage, and by week 6 the germ layers already exist and organs are forming.

questions.prompt: The liver, pancreas and the lining of the gut develop from
questions.explanation: The endoderm gives the lining of the digestive tract and its glands. The mesoderm gives muscle, bone and the heart.

questions.prompt: The notochord is important in early development because it

options.text: induces the overlying ectoderm to form the neural plate

questions.explanation: Signals from the notochord begin neurulation. In adults, remnants of the notochord persist as the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral discs. The placenta arises from the trophoblast and uterine tissue, and the heart tube arises from mesoderm.

questions.prompt: Failure of the posterior neuropore to close causes
questions.explanation: The posterior neuropore closes around day 27 and forms the lower spinal cord. Failure of the anterior neuropore leads to anencephaly.

questions.prompt: Taking which vitamin before conception and in early pregnancy reduces the risk of neural tube defects?
questions.explanation: Folic acid supplementation lowers the incidence of neural tube defects. High-dose vitamin A is itself teratogenic, so it is the wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Somites, which develop from paraxial mesoderm, give rise to

options.text: vertebrae, skeletal muscle and the dermis of the back

questions.explanation: Somites form the sclerotome (bone), myotome (muscle) and dermatome (dermis). The epidermis comes from ectoderm.

questions.prompt: The fetal part of the placenta is formed from the
questions.explanation: The chorion frondosum is the villous fetal part. The decidua basalis is the maternal part of the placenta.

questions.prompt: A normal umbilical cord contains
questions.explanation: The two arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta, and the single vein returns oxygenated blood. A single umbilical artery is associated with other anomalies.

questions.prompt: Polyhydramnios (excess amniotic fluid) is classically associated with

options.text: renal agenesis, because there is no fetal urine
oesophageal atresia, because the fetus cannot swallow fluid

questions.explanation: Swallowing normally helps to clear amniotic fluid, so its absence causes excess. Renal agenesis causes too little fluid, which is oligohydramnios.

questions.prompt: The period of greatest susceptibility of an embryo to teratogens is

options.text: weeks 3 to 8, the period of organogenesis

questions.explanation: Organs form during weeks 3 to 8, so exposure then causes major structural defects. In weeks 1 to 2, damage usually kills the embryo or is repaired (all-or-none). Later in pregnancy, exposure tends to disturb growth and function rather than cause major structural defects.
